_meta.indication: Beta-3 adrenergic agonist indicated for the treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group, multicenter trial; Study 1 included an active control (tolterodine ER 4 mg)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency for at least 3 months, with at least 8 micturitions per day and at least 3 episodes of urgency with or without incontinence over 3 days
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Final Visit (Week 12) in mean number of incontinence episodes per 24 hours (in subjects with incontinence at baseline) and mean number of micturitions per 24 hours
pivotal_trials.n: 1906 randomized (FAS): placebo 480, mirabegron 50 mg 473, mirabegron 100 mg 478, tolterodine SR 4 mg 475
pivotal_trials.result: Mirabegron 50 mg incontinence episodes adjusted mean difference vs placebo -0.41 (95% CI -0.72, -0.09; p=0.003); micturitions difference -0.60 (95% CI -0.90, -0.29; p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group, multicenter trial; patients randomized to placebo, mirabegron 25 mg or mirabegron 50 mg
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Week 12 in mean number of incontinence episodes per 24 hours and mean number of micturitions per 24 hours
pivotal_trials.n: Incontinence analysis placebo 262, mirabegron 25 mg 254, mirabegron 50 mg 257; micturitions placebo 415, mirabegron 25 mg 410, mirabegron 50 mg 426
pivotal_trials.result: Mirabegron 25 mg incontinence episodes difference vs placebo -0.40 (95% CI -0.74, -0.06; p=0.005) and 50 mg -0.42 (95% CI -0.76, -0.08; p=0.001); micturitions 25 mg -0.47 (95% CI -0.82, -0.13; p=0.007) and 50 mg -0.42 (95% CI -0.76, -0.08; p=0.015)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2% and >placebo) were hypertension (25 mg 11.3%, 50 mg 7.5% vs placebo 7.6%), nasopharyngitis (25 mg 3.5%, 50 mg 3.9% vs 2.5%), urinary tract infection (25 mg 4.2%, 50 mg 2.9% vs 1.8%) and headache (25 mg 2.1%, 50 mg 3.2% vs 3.0%); Myrbetriq can increase blood pressure
target_moa: Agonist for the human beta-3 adrenoceptor (beta-3-AR), the dominant subtype in the human detrusor muscle; activation relaxes the bladder during the filling phase and inhibits non-voiding activity, enhancing urine storage
modality: small molecule (new molecular entity, beta-3-adrenergic receptor agonist tablet)

advisory_committee.vote: On April 5, 2012 the Reproductive Health Drugs Advisory Committee voted on overall benefit-risk supporting approval: Yes 7, No 4, Abstain 1; on substantial evidence of benefit Yes 8, No 4; on adequate safety Yes 9, No 3

description.text: Added co-administration of mirabegron with solifenacin succinate for overactive bladder with urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the co-administration therapy of MYRBETRIQ® with solifenacin succinate for the treatment of overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency.

description.text: Added treatment of neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) in pediatric patients 3 years and older weighing 35 kg or more

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the treatment of neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) in pediatric patients 3 years and older and weighing 35 kilograms or more.

summary.text: Standard NDA under 505(b) for a first-in-class new molecular entity (beta-3-adrenergic agonist), received August 29, 2011 with a PDUFA goal date of June 29, 2012 and approved June 29, 2012 on first cycle; reviewed with a Reproductive Health Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on April 5, 2012; approval included required postmarketing cardiovascular and malignancy observational studies and deferred pediatric studies

citations.quote: Astellas Pharma US, Inc. submitted an NDA (202-611) for a new molecular entity containing a proposed beta-3-adrenergic receptor (\beta 3-AR) agonist in a tablet formulation. The active ingredient is mirabegron (trade name Myrbetriq). Mirabegron is indicated for the treatment of overactive bladder. Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated August 26, 2011, received August 29, 2011, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Myrbetriq (mirabegron), 25 mg and 50 mg extended release tablets.
Date of receipt of original submission	August 29, 2011

On April 5, 2012 a Reproductive Health Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was held to discuss the efficacy and safety data for mirabegron as a new molecular entity. The focus of the discussion included the efficacy of the product, the blood pressure findings from phase 1 and 3 studies, the increased reports of neoplasms at the 100 mg dose, identified hepatic adverse events and hypersensitivity reactions. A summary of the Committee voting on the following three questions is outlined below:

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study 1898-1: open label, multicenter single ascending dose PK/safety study of mirabegron suspension in children 5 to less than 18 years with NDO or OAB

citations.quote: 1898-1 Open label, multicenter single ascending dose study to evaluate pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of mirabegron modified release microgranule-based suspension in children from 5 to less than 18 years of age with neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) or overactive bladder (OAB).

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study 1898-2: open label, dose titration study evaluating PK, safety and efficacy of mirabegron suspension in children 5 to less than 18 years with NDO

citations.quote: 1898-2 Open label, baseline-controlled, multicenter, sequential dose titration study followed by a fixed dose observation period to evaluate pharmacokinetics, safety and efficacy of mirabegron modified release microgranule-based suspension in children from 5 to less than 18 years of age with NDO.

requirement.text: 505(o) study 1898-3: long-term observational study in US and European electronic healthcare databases to evaluate the incidence of serious cardiovascular outcomes in patients administered Myrbetriq

citations.quote: 1898-3 A long-term observational study using electronic healthcare databases with appropriate linkages conducted in United States and European databases to evaluate the incidence of serious cardiovascular outcomes (both individual and composite outcomes) in patients administered Myrbetriq (mirabegron).
